detailed_findings.finding: The proof correctly characterizes membership in S_x in each residue class modulo m.
The argument that the gaps are exactly the listed finite sets and are pairwise disjoint is correct and sufficient to compute the genus.
There is no substantive semantic drift: the lemma proved matches the stated genus formula and aligns with the root theorem's Kunz-coordinate framework.

reason: The proof gives a complete residue-class analysis of the set S_x. For residue 0, all multiples of m are in S_x. For each residue i in {1,...,m-1}, it correctly identifies the elements of S_x with that residue as exactly {t m + i : t >= x_i}, so the missing elements in that residue class are exactly i, m+i, ..., (x_i-1)m+i, numbering x_i many. These gap sets are disjoint by residue class, and summing their sizes gives the genus. The note that Kunz inequalities are not used in the counting argument is semantically acceptable: they are only needed to ensure S_x is a numerical semigroup in the broader correspondence.
